opening:
The young woman was stopped at the baggage security checkpoint.
She said, "My luggage contains only pajamas, a pillow, a thermos, a towel, and some changes of clothes—why are you stopping me?"
After inspecting her luggage, security personnel handcuffed her and took her away.
solution:
The man the girl loved betrayed her today; he was packing his bags, preparing to move out of the apartment they shared.
The girl tearfully begged him not to leave, but he did not look back.
Just then, the girl said coldly, "At least leave my pillow behind."
And so, she cut off the boy's hand.
The "pillow" she wanted to keep was his hand, a body part she treated as her pillow/headrest. She carried the severed hand in her luggage and called it her pillow. At the baggage checkpoint, security personnel discovered the human hand, handcuffed her and took her away.
source: User-supplied opening and final answer; explicit user requirement: full narrative and hand, not arm. Source URL unknown.
source_solution_verbatim:
The man the girl loved betrayed her today; he was packing his bags, preparing to move out of the apartment they shared.
The girl tearfully begged him not to leave, but he did not look back.
Just then, the girl said coldly, "At least leave my pillow behind."
And so, she cut off the boy's hand.
source_reconciliation: The last paragraph connects the supplied opening to its supplied answer. Pillow/headrest usage is supported by the reference exchange but normalised to HAND under the user's explicit correction. Security discovers the hand as the explanation for detention. Details of wrapping, a separate stabbing, outcome of the injury and type of betrayal are not invented.
canonical_facts: The woman and the man were romantic partners and shared an apartment.
He betrayed her that day, and he was packing his bags to move out of their shared apartment.
She tearfully begged him not to leave. He did not look back or accept her plea.
She then said coldly, "At least leave my pillow behind."
She deliberately severed his hand to keep the body part she treated as her pillow/headrest.
The body part in this version is a HAND, not an arm. Arm and hand are not interchangeable terms in this story.
The item she called a pillow in her luggage was that severed human hand.
At a baggage security checkpoint, personnel inspected the luggage, discovered the hand, and handcuffed and took her away.
Her list was pajamas, a pillow, a thermos, a towel and changes of clothes. The hidden bodily referent is the pillow, not the other listed items.
explicit_negatives: The pillow in the twist was not an ordinary stuffed cushion, a prosthetic, or an animal body part.
She did not sever or carry a whole arm as the pillow; this story specifies the hand.
The severing was not an accident, self-defence, a medical amputation or a consensual gift.
An unrelated travel restriction on an ordinary pillow, a liquid-limit issue, a concealed drug shipment or an ordinary stolen cushion does not explain her detention.
The other listed items were not made from the partner's body parts.
unknown_details: The precise type of betrayal is unspecified; do not assume an affair.
Whether the man died, the injury details, the precise implement and any distinct stabbing event are unspecified.
Whether the hand was wrapped, placed in a pillowcase or visually disguised is unspecified. Calling it a pillow does not prove a visual disguise.
The checkpoint transport mode, city, travel destination and exact time after the apartment incident are unspecified.
Which hand, the ages of the characters, the exact duration of their relationship and legal charges are unspecified.
